slot: Income tax: 44ADA / 44AD -> Section 58 of Income-tax Act 2025 (VERIFY WITH A CA)

pick.name: Presumptive taxation under s.58 (old 44ADA for consulting; old 44AD for SaaS/product income)
pick.what: Income-tax Act 2025 in force from 1 April 2026 (tax year 2026-27); 44AD/44AE/44ADA are now s.58(2) Table Sl. 1/2/3
pick.why: Consulting = 'information technology' notified profession -> 50% deemed profit, no books; SaaS subscriptions are likely BUSINESS income -> 6% of digital receipts deemed profit
pick.free_limits: Profession (Sl.3): receipts <= Rs50 lakh, Rs75 lakh if cash <= 5%, 50% deemed. Business (Sl.1): turnover <= Rs2 crore, Rs3 crore if cash <= 5%, 6% of digital/banking receipts (8% otherwise). Residents (individual/HUF/firm), not LLPs. Presumptive taxpayers pay 100% advance tax by 15 March. s.58 reportedly disqualifies specified professionals from Sl.1 assessee-wide.

alts.name: Regular books (ITR-3 equivalent)
alts.why: When expenses > presumptive margin or mixed income disqualifies s.58

alts.name: Company taxation
alts.why: When raising money or for enterprise contracts

candidates.name: Old 44AD (Sl.1) for all income
candidates.verdict: Only if you have no professional/consulting income; CA to confirm

decision: For services/consulting, presumptive 50% (old 44ADA) is the simplest. If SaaS product revenue grows, 6% presumptive business income (old 44AD) is very attractive, but mixing professional and business income may disqualify you under the new s.58, so get a CA to structure it (sometimes by separating the product into a firm/company).
details: Sources: TaxGuru s.58 analysis + mapping tables; Deccan Herald/CBDT press release (1 Apr 2026 commencement, incometaxindia.gov.in PDF returned 403 to fetch); IT notified under s.44AA per Notification 116/F.No.23/FB/2001-TPL (secondary). VERIFY WITH A CA.

verify.note: Official: incometax.gov.in (Oct 2026 news items) confirms the Income-tax Act 2025 is operative for 'Tax Year 2026-27 onwards' (payments, TDS statements, a 27 Oct 2026 CBDT notification). NOT officially confirmed: the s.58 table (50%/Rs50L-75L profession; 6%/8%, Rs2-3 crore business), the specified-professional exclusion from Sl.1, LLP exclusion, and the 15-March advance-tax rule under the new Act. All are from TaxGuru only (incometaxindia.gov.in returns 403; indiacode 403). TaxGuru does state the Sl.1 exclusion for specified professionals, which supports the 'mixing' warning. Keep VERIFY WITH A CA.
